about: Vectors for the x402/exact/tron/lcp-trc20-memo pairing: the tron entry point of @integraledger/lcp. H is SHA-256("abc") from FIPS 180-2. V1 is mainnet transaction 40662c9c…, read live from a Solidity node. V2's inputs are the published Anvil development key, USDT-TRC20, the payee bytes of x402's example option under 0x41, and solidified block 86542765. The signature was made with coincurve 21.0.0 (RFC 6979) and recovers to the payer; base58check with base58 2.1.1; the Transfer topic with pycryptodome 3.23.0 keccak; every SHA-256 with hashlib. Negative transactions are V2 with fields changed, written by hand from Tron.proto's field numbers. V4's status fixtures model the nodes' answers: a lookup that finds nothing answers notFound with the time of the latest block at its level on the node that answered, and null marks an answer status does not read. A node includes a transaction only while its expiration is after the head block's time (java-tron Manager.validateCommon), so a lookup names absence through the solid head read first only when its node has reached that head's time. V4's recover fixtures model the transaction read's answers: a transaction id is the SHA-256 of its raw data, so raw data whose SHA-256 is another is not the transaction the id names, an answer recover refuses tron/unreadable as it refuses a failed read. Byte strings are lowercase hex; int64 values are decimal strings. V4's status rows and the plant are read with the act payment at the finality the row gives, solidified where it gives none, after the position the row gives, and answer as the profile read-status gives them with the pairing's rule 8: each reference holds V2's raw data, the payment presented. Status rows read the transaction's owner, the reference's payer, against the option's payee, and record each Transfer log of the receipt whose sender, the address its second topic names, is the transaction's owner (its emitter, the recipient its third topic names and the amount its data holds, the data written for these modeled answers from the amount V2 signs; the topics as TRC-20's Transfer(address indexed _from, address indexed _to, uint256 _value) orders them, tronprotocol/tips at c29d7363, tip-20.md:159) as what moved, named by the id and the log's place among the receipt's logs; an answer that names a transaction names its owner as the signer and its contract's Permission_id (Tron.proto:384 at java-tron 4e8389f1; 0 where absent, as protobuf omits a default) as the authority; on the act payment the transaction is the payment only where a log's recipient is payTo, whatever contract emitted it. Block answers are constructed, in the shape java-tron at 4e8389f1 gives (framework/src/main/java/org/tron/core/services/http/GetBlockByLimitNextServlet.java:18, :45-52; Util.java:137-148, :295-298): each block is named by its number, the 8 bytes a blockID begins with, then the bytes ab, its parentHash the block before it's. A failed receipt, a receipt that names no payee's account and a lapse take the search for H, and until the run that shows a block's answer lists every transaction of its block a complete search proves no absence: they answer pending search-incomplete, with the search's position where it had a range (rule 25). V5's rows read the search over constructed blocks whose transactions are V2's raw data with fields changed by hand (its timestamp, its owner, its call's recipient), each id their SHA-256 by hashlib. zero's rows read a signed transfer(to, 0) whose receipt holds no Transfer log, as its case states. owner's rows read V4's raw data, or zero's, under receipts whose Transfer logs come from the owner and from another account, the other account 0x41 and twenty 0x11 bytes and the third 0x41 and twenty 0x22 bytes: only the owner's logs are what moved, and the transfer of zero is read only from a receipt that holds no Transfer log.

V2.case: build({required: {x402Version: 2, resource, accepts: [O]}, accepted: O, payer, refBlock, now, feeLimit}, H), then complete(signature). expectRawHex is Transaction.raw encoded by hand from TRON's protobuf schema (tronprotocol/protocol 8432beca, core/Tron.proto L431-445 Transaction.raw and L336-385 Transaction.Contract, core/contract/smart_contract.proto L74-81 TriggerSmartContract; google.protobuf.Any from protocolbuffers/protobuf v29.3, src/google/protobuf/any.proto L128-162) in the protobuf wire format (protobuf.dev/programming-guides/encoding), each field in field-number order and none at its default value: ref_block_bytes (1) bytes 6 to 8 of refBlock.number as 8 big-endian bytes and ref_block_hash (4) bytes 8 to 16 of refBlock.id, as java-tron's TransactionCapsule.setReference takes them (tronprotocol/java-tron 5c449a18, chainbase/src/main/java/org/tron/core/capsule/TransactionCapsule.java L519-526); expiration (8) now + maxTimeoutSeconds × 1000; data (10) the 77 ASCII bytes lcp:sha256: followed by H; contract (11) one Contract of type (1) 31, TriggerSmartContract, and parameter (2) an Any of type_url (1) type.googleapis.com/protocol.TriggerSmartContract and value (2) the TriggerSmartContract of owner_address (1) payerBytes, contract_address (2) assetBytes and data (4) the calldata; timestamp (14) now; fee_limit (18) feeLimit. The calldata is eth-abi 6.0.0's encode of ["address", "uint256"] with the last 20 bytes of payToBytes and amount, after eth-utils 6.0.0's selector of transfer(address,uint256), and in the test viem 2.57.4's encodeFunctionData of erc20Abi's transfer. expectTxid is the SHA-256 of expectRawHex, java-tron's transaction id (TransactionCapsule.java getTransactionId L721-726 and getRawHash L584-587), computed with hashlib and node:crypto. expectTransactionHex, the transaction in expectPayload, is Transaction encoded by hand from the same schema (core/Tron.proto L447-449): raw_data (1) expectRawHex, signature (2) expectSignature.

agreedRefusals.about: Refusal codes where the pairing leaves the code to the implementation. The TypeScript and Python implementations both apply every row but the recover rows, which the TypeScript implementation alone applies: the Python one has no recover. A transaction's length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's String length counts it; U+10000 is one code point of two UTF-16 code units.

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.

zero.case: A transaction of the form whose signed call is transfer(to, 0) and whose receipt, SUCCESS, holds no Transfer log, as a token that logs nothing for zero answers: V2's raw data with the call's amount word zeroed (zero) or its recipient the account 0x41 and twenty 0x11 bytes and its amount zeroed (other), by hand, each id its SHA-256 by hashlib. Each row's reference is V4's with the row's raw data and id. What moved is that call's transfer of zero to its to, named by the id and the place call; on the act payment it is the payment where that to is payTo (the profile's rule 8). The other account's is read at the solidified level with no position given, so its search for H has no range: pending search-incomplete, the transaction named a foreign item, other-account.

owner.case: Receipts whose Transfer logs come from the owner and from another account: what moved is each log whose sender is the owner, at its own place among the receipt's logs, and a signed transfer(to, 0) is a transfer of zero only where the receipt holds no Transfer log at all.

rows.case: a log from another account to payTo and the owner's log to a third account: the owner's alone moved, at place 1; it names another account than payTo, so it is not the payment: a foreign item, other-account, with no range to search search-incomplete
the owner's log to payTo and a log from another account to a third account: settled, the owner's log alone recorded, the owner the signer and Permission_id 0 the authority
